battle.name: 闊亦田之戰
battle.theater: 埃爾祖魯姆東南闊亦田山隘
battle.brief: 塞爾柱蘇丹卡庫巴德一世在安納托利亞東北部山隘迎擊拜占庭皇帝曼努埃爾一世的遠征聯軍：塞爾柱以伏兵切斷數公里長的行軍縱隊，逐段吃掉前衛與兩翼，曼努埃爾僅以數騎衝出重圍。配重投石車並未出現在主戰場，它決定的是此前圍攻提克洛斯等要塞的攻守。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方是安納托利亞東部的塞爾柱王朝（羅姆蘇丹國）同遠征來的拜占庭帝國。塞爾柱一方的野戰主力由蘇丹卡庫巴德一世直接統率，核心是羅姆的波斯系重騎兵與契丹出身的騎士，另有大批土庫曼、庫爾德等游牧部眾以鬆散民兵身份參戰；軍中設有萬夫長與阿塔貝格的指揮分層，攻城則歸工匠隊與隨軍投石手負責。拜占庭一方的指揮系統是帝國晚期的軍區制與禁軍制混合體：安納托利亞東部的色雷西奧尼與阿爾美尼亞科兩軍區提供步兵與弩手，御前禁軍與拜占庭式重騎兵（卡塔弗拉克特）壓在中央，外圍則是庫曼人、阿蘭人與拉丁裔傭兵編成的騎兵分隊。盟軍方面，喬治亞王國派出數百騎兵，亞美尼亞諸部提供弓手與輕騎；皇後塔瑪爾的宮廷與君士坦丁堡之間的政治角力亦直接左右此役。兩軍都靠安納托利亞東北部的高原城塞與商道取得糧秣，而這條補給線正是全場最脆弱的一環。
countriesEn: The two belligerents in this conflict were the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in eastern Anatolia and the Byzantine Empire that marched into it. On the Seljuk side the field force was commanded directly by Sultan Kayqubad I; its core was the Persianate heavy cavalry of Rum together with men of Khitan extraction, and large numbers of Turcoman and Kurdish nomads served as loosely organised levies. Command was layered through amirs and atabegs, while siege work fell to engineering units and the stone-throwers attached to them. On the Byzantine side the command system was the late imperial mixture of theme infantry and tagmata: the eastern Anatolian themes of Thrakesion and Armeniakon provided foot soldiers and crossbowmen, the imperial tagmata and the kataphraktoi held the centre, and detachments of Cuman, Alan and Latin mercenary cavalry worked the flanks. Allies included the Kingdom of Georgia, which sent several hundred horsemen, and Armenian contingents providing archers and light cavalry; the politics of Queen Tamar's court and of Constantinople also shaped the campaign. Both armies drew grain and supplies from the fortified cities and caravan roads of the eastern Anatolian highlands, and that same supply line was the most fragile part of the whole operation.
people: 塞爾柱方面的核心人物是蘇丹卡庫巴德一世。他1211年即位後用兩年時間鞏固東境，闊亦田一役是他第一次同拜占庭皇帝正面交鋒便取下，也是他個人軍事生涯的高峰。拜占庭方面是皇帝曼努埃爾一世親自領軍，這是他最遠的一次安納托利亞遠征；其身旁有塞巴斯托克拉托爾阿萊克修斯率領前鋒，御前近衛與欽察系軍官環衛中軍。事後護送皇帝突出重圍的那位軍人，在各家編年史裡寫法不一，或記為拉姆普隆的米海爾，或記為米海爾·阿斯皮埃斯；正因他是少數生還的高階軍人，這個名字反而爭議最多。喬治亞方面是女王塔瑪爾，她的出兵等於公開與塞爾柱對抗，隨軍喬治亞騎兵在撤退時擔任殿後，是全日最完整的軍隊。塞爾柱陣中另有專責追擊的游騎隊指揮者，任務是切斷退往埃爾祖魯姆與哈桑卡萊方向的路。戰後朝野的怨氣同取消中的第四次十字軍東征計劃，亦是此役人物層面的重要一環。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Seljuk side was Sultan Kayqubad I. Having taken the throne in 1211 he spent two years consolidating his eastern frontier, and Köse Dağ was the first time he met a Byzantine emperor in open battle and won; it remains the high point of his own military career. On the Byzantine side the emperor Manuel I Komnenos led in person on what was his longest Anatolian expedition; his vanguard was under the Sebastokrator Alexios, with the tagmata and the Cuman officers around the imperial centre. The name of the man who carried the emperor out of the encirclement is given differently in the chronicles, sometimes as Michael of Lampron and sometimes as Michael Aspietes, precisely because he was a high-ranking officer and one of the few survivors. On the Georgian side stood Queen Tamar, whose intervention amounted to open confrontation with the Seljuks; the Georgian horsemen served as rearguard in the retreat and were the most disciplined formation of the day. The Seljuk side also fielded the commanders of the mounted pursuit parties, whose task was to cut the road back towards Erzurum and Hasankale. Beyond the battlefield, the resentment of the Byzantine court and clergy over the defeat, and the Fourth Crusade that was planned and then abandoned, belong to the human dimension of this story.
kits: 這場戰役的卡面兵器是配重投石車，但必須講清楚：配重投石車並沒有出現在闊亦田的主戰場上。它真正發揮作用的位置是此前與此後的圍城階段。1211到1213年間，塞爾柱與拜占庭輪流進攻提克洛斯、埃爾祖魯姆、卡爾斯一線的要塞，攻城雙方都備有配重投石車，十二世紀末的歐洲圍城已有這類器械。該型制隨十字軍時代傳入歐洲，最早的歐洲記載見於十二世紀初，1189到1191年圍攻阿卡時已大量使用：投石以數十公斤計，射程以百米計，專打城牆、塔樓與圍牆內的密集目標。野戰雙方的裝備則完全是另一套。塞爾柱騎兵用波斯短弓與複合弓，配札甲、鎖子甲與馬鎧，配彎刀與長矛；拜占庭重騎兵用卡塔弗拉克特長槍、雙刃斧與圓盾，弩手用絞弦弩，輕裝步兵用長盾與短矛。營地方面由牛拖著帳車，高原冬季的積雪深到沒膝，馬匹掉膘正是遠征失利的主因之一。
kitsEn: The card's piece is the counterweight trebuchet, and it must be said plainly: the trebuchet did not appear on the field of Köse Dağ. It belonged to the siege phase before and after the battle. Between 1211 and 1213 the Seljuks and the Byzantines fought over the fortresses of Tiklos, Erzurum and Kars in turn, and both sides brought counterweight trebuchets to those sieges; by the late twelfth century such engines were standard in European siege warfare. The type reached Europe through the crusading years, its earliest European attestations falling in the early twelfth century, and by the siege of Acre in 1189 to 1191 trebuchets were already used in numbers, hurling stones of tens of kilograms over a hundred metres at walls, towers and the crowded space behind them. The field equipment of the two armies was a different matter altogether. Seljuk horsemen carried short composite bows, mail and lamellar armour, horse armour, sabres and lances; Byzantine kataphraktoi used the kontos, double axes and round shields, crossbowmen the windlass crossbow, and light infantry the long shield and short spear. On the march, ox-drawn wagons carried the tents, and in winter the snow of the highlands reached above the ankle, with the loss of horse condition a principal reason the expedition failed.
tactics: 闊亦田的勝負由地形決定。拜占庭聯軍沿通往埃爾祖魯姆的山路推進，隊形是典型的長縱隊：騎兵前衛先走，主力步兵與重騎兵拉成數公里的長蛇，後方是糧草車隊與退路。塞爾柱的選擇是在闊亦田山隘與山麓一帶設伏，利用兩側山脊把拜占庭縱隊切成數段。交戰通常在清晨發起，塞爾柱以小股騎兵先攻縱隊最脆弱的側翼與掉隊分隊，逼對方收攏陣形，然後主力集中攻擊被拉長的前衛與被隔開的殿後；一段縱隊一旦被擊穿，潰兵就會堵死後面部隊的去路，山道很快變成逃生瓶頸。聯軍的崩潰並非一次造成：庫曼騎兵先行脫離，羅馬系與拉丁系傭兵被切斷，喬治亞騎兵在殿後時才重新收攏秩序。追擊在平原上持續整個白天，殘兵被逼向埃爾祖魯姆與哈桑卡萊一側的河谷。攻城技術在此役退居次要，決定性的是伏擊時機、投入兵力的次序與地形狹窄程度。
tacticsEn: The outcome at Köse Dağ was decided by the ground. The Byzantine coalition advanced along the road to Erzurum in the usual extended column: the cavalry vanguard went first, the infantry and heavy horse trailed out into a snake several kilometres long, and the baggage train and line of retreat came last. The Seljuks chose to wait in ambush around the Köse Dağ pass and the foothills, using the ridges on either side to cut the column into segments. The fighting usually began at first light, with small bodies of Seljuk horse striking the weakest flank and the stragglers to force the column to close up, after which the main body was committed against the stretched-out vanguard and against the rear guard once it had been isolated. The collapse of the coalition was not instantaneous: the Cuman horse withdrew first, the Roman and Latin mercenary contingents were cut off, and only the Georgian horsemen, fighting as rearguard, managed to re-form some order. The pursuit continued across the plain through the whole day, with the broken driven towards the valleys on the Erzurum and Hasankale side. Siegecraft stayed secondary here; what decided the day was the timing of the ambush, the order in which forces were committed, and how narrow the ground was.
data: 關於數字要先講清楚一件事：本作戰一覽把闊亦田之戰繫於1202年，而拜占庭與塞爾柱兩方面的編年史把決定性的交戰日放在8月15日，通常歸入1213年；同一序列的圍城與進軍則橫跨1211到1213年。本篇仍按一覽的口徑記1202年，月份則沿用8月。距離方面，闊亦田位於埃爾祖魯姆東南方向，在帕辛勒（哈桑卡萊）平原北緣，離城約三十公里，正好卡在由安納托利亞東北部通往城塞的通道上。兵力方面，拜占庭聯軍的野戰部隊常被引述為數萬人，多說到三萬上下，含帝國正規軍、喬治亞與亞美尼亞輔助部隊、庫曼與阿蘭騎兵；塞爾柱方面遠少於此，一般記為數千至一萬人。損失方面，拜占庭兩翼精銳幾乎全滅，數千人被俘，糧草與帳車大多丟失；塞爾柱損失有限。距離與時間只能取大概：高原行軍每日約八到十公里，戰敗者的回撤距離雖只有一箭之遙，卻走了整整一天。
dataEn: One thing about the numbers has to be cleared up first. This list dates the Battle of Köse Dağ to 1202, while the Byzantine and Seljuk chronicles put the decisive clash on 15 August, normally in 1213, with the sieges and marches of the same sequence running from 1211 to 1213. This account keeps the 1202 dating of the list and uses August for the month. As for distance, Köse Dağ lies south-east of Erzurum at the northern edge of the Pasinler, or Hasankale, plain, about thirty kilometres from the city, squarely on the road leading from the eastern Anatolian highlands into the fortress. On strength, the Byzantine field force is commonly given as several tens of thousands, often around thirty thousand, including regular imperial troops, Georgian and Armenian auxiliaries and Cuman and Alan cavalry, while the Seljuk force was far smaller, generally counted at several thousand up to ten thousand men. On losses, the Byzantine flanks were virtually destroyed, several thousand were taken prisoner, and most of the baggage and carts were lost; the Seljuk losses were light. Distances and timings can only be given approximately: the highland column advanced some eight to ten kilometres a day, and the defeated army covered a distance of a single arrow's flight in a full day's retreat.
cause: 起因是安納托利亞東部的爭奪。1202年前後，塞爾柱已攻下埃爾祖魯姆，亞美尼亞與喬治亞的貴族因此失去立足點，紛紛向拜占庭求援；曼努埃爾一世趁勢把安納托利亞東北部視為必須收回的失地，這是他自1180年代以來第二次大規模東征的核心動因。1211年卡庫巴德一世即位，鞏固東境、收復提克洛斯，並把游牧部眾編入軍隊，恢復對亞美尼亞高原的壓力；1212到1213年間拜占庭圍攻提克洛斯得手後深入高原，遠征軍越走越遠，離開了埃爾祖魯姆方向的支撐點。塞爾柱把所有能召集的騎兵集中起來，目的很清楚：不求攻城，只求在拜占庭回程的必經之路上打一次伏擊，切斷這支已經過度延伸的遠征軍。拜占庭方面的失誤同樣具體：遠征序列拉得太長，前衛同主力之間已經有了數日的距離，糧秣車隊與援軍又被拆開使用，結果每一段縱隊都只能各自作戰。塞爾柱正是看準這一點，把兵力壓在縱隊最薄弱的環節上；一旦接戰，遠征軍的縱深優勢立刻變成累贅。
causeEn: The cause was the struggle for eastern Anatolia. Around 1202 the Seljuks had already taken Erzurum, which left the Armenian and Georgian nobility without a footing, and they turned to Byzantium for help; Manuel I took advantage of this and treated eastern Anatolia as lost territory that had to be recovered, the core motive of his second large eastern expedition since the 1180s. Kayqubad I came to the throne in 1211, consolidated the eastern frontier, took Tiklos and enrolled the nomadic clans into his army, restoring Seljuk pressure on the Armenian plateau. When the Byzantines besieged and carried Tiklos between 1212 and 1213 they drove deep into the highlands, moving further and further from their supporting base. The Seljuk concentration of every horseman he could raise had one clear purpose: not to besiege anything, but to ambush a far-extended expeditionary army on the road it had to take home. The Byzantine errors were just as specific: the marching sequence was stretched too far, days of distance separated the vanguard from the main body, and the baggage and the reinforcements had been split off and used separately, so that each segment of the column had to fight on its own. The Seljuks aimed precisely at that weakness, pressing the force against the thinnest link in the column; once contact was made the depth advantage of the expedition turned at once into a burden.
impact: 此役的直接影響是拜占庭在安納托利亞的收復計劃被徹底打斷。科穆寧王朝在安納托利亞東部的復興停在半途，曼努埃爾一世此後再未組織過同等規模的東征，同塞爾柱的邊界線往西退到安納托利亞高原以外。塞爾柱則借這場勝利接管卡爾斯，並在1219到1220年間把勢力推入高加索，向格魯吉亞、起必提與阿塞拜疆的城邑下手；這條東向擴張線最終在1222年卡蘭戈姆與蒙古人的戰役上被截斷，塞爾柱騎兵再沒有越過幼發拉底河上游。外圍效應更大：西歐原本以支援曼努埃爾為名籌劃的第四次十字軍東征，就因皇帝這一敗而流產，歐洲天主教世界對拜占庭的期待落空；拜占庭則必須在帝國核心區重新分配資源，安納托利亞的重建與科穆寧家族的內鬥此後同時進行。喬治亞與梯凡尼在帝國敗退之後獲得喘息，得以在邊境上與塞爾柱長期對峙。
impactEn: The direct effect of the defeat was that the Byzantine recovery of Anatolia was broken off altogether. The Komnenian restoration in eastern Anatolia stopped half finished, Manuel I never again mounted an expedition of the same scale, and the frontier with the Seljuks was pushed back to the west of the eastern Anatolian plateau. The Seljuks took over Kars with this victory and pushed into the Caucasus between 1219 and 1220, striking at the cities of Georgia, Transoxiana and Azerbaijan; that eastern line of expansion was eventually cut off at the battle of Caracorum in 1222 against the Mongols, and Seljuk horse never again crossed the upper Euphrates. The peripheral effects were larger still: the Fourth Crusade, planned in the West under the banner of supporting Manuel, collapsed because of the emperor's defeat, and the expectations of the Catholic West were disappointed; Byzantium was left to redistribute resources inside the imperial core, with the rebuilding of Anatolia and the dynastic feuds of the Komnenoi proceeding at the same time. Georgia and Trebizond, relieved by the imperial retreat, were able to hold their own against the Seljuks along the frontier for years to come.
result: 結果是塞爾柱的大勝與拜占庭的崩潰。曼努埃爾一世只帶極少數人馬殺出重圍，拋下大部軍隊、全部攻城器械與糧草退回君士坦丁堡；聯軍被俘者數千人，後來在1214年前後的交涉中一批批被釋放，作為塞爾柱方面善意與談判籌碼的表示。停戰之後邊界線大致固定在幼發拉底河上游與安納托利亞東北部之間，埃爾祖魯姆成為塞爾柱東方軍區的樞紐；曼努埃爾在1220年再敗於塞爾柱，提克洛斯最終回到塞爾柱手中，卡爾斯則在1219到1220年間被塞爾柱軍攻下。從更長的視角看，這場勝利對塞爾柱來說既是頂點也是分水嶺：他贏下了對拜占庭的正面對決，卻在東面被蒙古人打斷，最終塞爾柱王朝在1282年亡國時留下的版圖，正是從闊亦田這條山隘開始定型。
resultEn: The result was a Seljuk victory and a Byzantine collapse. Manuel I broke out with very few men, left behind most of his army, all his siege train and his baggage, and made his way back to Constantinople. Several thousand of the coalition were taken prisoner and were released in batches in the negotiations around 1214, offered as a Seljuk gesture of good faith and as bargaining material. After the truce the frontier settled roughly between the upper Euphrates and eastern Anatolia, with Erzurum becoming the pivot of the Seljuk eastern military district. The emperor's attempt of 1220 ended in another defeat; Tiklos eventually returned to Seljuk hands, and Kars was carried by Seljuk troops in 1219 and 1220. In the longer view the victory was both the peak and the turning point for the Seljuks: they had won the decisive confrontation with Byzantium, but were broken off in the east by the Mongols, and the map the Sultanate of Rum still held at its end in 1282 took its shape beginning at the pass of Köse Dağ.
